headline: Ivanti gateways lead a day of AI-wrapped attacker tooling
standfirst: CISA confirms in-the-wild exploitation of an Ivanti Connect Secure flaw, Anthropic researchers build a remote-root Linux exploit, and several reports trace AI through both attacker and defender tooling.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Ivanti Connect Secure flaws were added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on evidence of active exploitation, with reporting describing attackers chaining three bugs to reach root on internet-facing gateways [[s8]]. Only one is identified in the supplied material: CVE-2026-111357, carried there at CVSS 8.8 as a missing-authentication flaw. The NVD record for the same CVE is lower and narrower — 7.0 High, CWE-829, a local vector needing low privileges and no user interaction — describing 22.8R2.4 mishandling how the dsinvoked broker trusts DSCache configuration data to escalate to root, exploited in the wild. The 8.8 unauthenticated-network framing and the 7.0 local vector are unreconciled in the supplied text; treat the entry path as unconfirmed. Configurations run from 25.1.0.0 up to below 25.1.1.3, plus 22.8 R2 through R2.5. CISA's required action and due date bind federal agencies under a directive, not every operator.

## Vulnerabilities

Researchers built a working exploit for a critical Linux kernel flaw in Multipath TCP that yields root-level remote command execution against servers exposing MPTCP listeners, with no authentication required [[s12]]. No CVE or version range is supplied, so triage starts from an inventory of hosts with MPTCP enabled rather than from a patch list.

## Breaches

Chainalysis disclosed a breach in which attackers used what it called "offensive agentic techniques" to reach internal systems and tools, exposing customer names, email addresses, user IDs and organisational roles [[s4]]. Analysis: the data is low-sensitivity identity material, but the method — described in the vendor's own words and not independently verified — is the point when the victim is a security vendor.

## Research

A crafted ChatGPT share link could run attacker code inside the logged-in session of anyone who opened it and expose private conversations; the researchers reported it through a bug bounty, and it was rated P1 and fixed within eight days [[s9]]. Share surfaces are the under-watched edge of assistant security: a link is the delivery mechanism, and trust in a familiar domain is the precondition.

CrowdStrike attributes a Go-based, AI-powered penetration-testing framework called ARTEX to a China-based targeted intrusion adversary it tracks as Vapor Panda, used against more than 200 organisations [[s17]]. A malicious Claude Code–branded extension, analysed alongside detection and remediation guidance, plants a persistent SSH backdoor [[s11]]. Analysis: both ride legitimate developer and AI workflows, so extension and package provenance plus SSH persistence hunting are the levers.

Talos shows the self-deleting VOLTA infostealer taking credentials, sessions and crypto wallets, then using LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets [[s6]]. Ranking inside the stealer collapses the gap between collection and monetisation.

## Industry

A court sentenced Syrian hacker Ahmad Umar Agha to 42 months for pro-Assad attacks on media, businesses and government entities, after more than a decade on the run [[s7]]. The supplied detail does not map the sentence to specific campaigns.

kev.shortDescription: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.

selected.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
selected.excerpt: Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners. [...]
selected.angle: Anthropic researchers built a working exploit for a critical Linux kernel MPTCP flaw that yields remote root on unauthenticated servers, putting patch urgency on any host exposing MPTCP listeners.

selected.title: Chainalysis discloses data breach from "offensive agentic techniques"
selected.excerpt: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed a data breach after attackers used "offensive agentic techniques" to access internal systems and tools, exposing customer names, email addresses, user IDs, and organizational roles. [...]
selected.angle: Chainalysis says attackers used 'offensive agentic techniques' to reach internal tools and customer identity data — a notable case of AI-driven intrusion against a security vendor itself.

selected.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
selected.excerpt: A malicious ChatGPT share link could run an attacker's code in the logged-in session of anyone who opened it, allowing them to read their private conversations, researchers at the security firm Parameter showed. The researchers reported the flaw through OpenAI's bug bounty program on October 18, and OpenAI fixed it eight days later and rated it P1, its most serious category.
selected.angle: A crafted ChatGPT share link could execute attacker code inside a logged-in session and expose private chats; OpenAI rated it P1 and fixed it in eight days, but it shows how share surfaces widen AI assistant attack surface.

selected.angle: CrowdStrike attributes a Go-based, AI-powered pentest framework called ARTEX to Chinese state-sponsored Vapor Panda, used against 200+ high-value targets — evidence of adversaries industrializing AI tooling.

selected.title: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
selected.excerpt: Microsoft analyzes a malicious Claude Code–branded extension, its persistent SSH backdoor, and guidance to detect and remediate it. The post Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.
selected.angle: Microsoft dissects a Claude Code-branded malicious extension that plants a persistent SSH backdoor, a concrete detection-and-remediation guide for the fast-growing AI developer-tool supply chain risk.

selected.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
selected.excerpt: The self-deleting VOLTA infostealer steals credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Then, it uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.
selected.angle: Talos shows the self-deleting VOLTA infostealer using LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets, shifting stealer tradecraft from bulk collection to prioritized targeting.
